lee: Quick sync: customer hit double side-effects when streaming client reconnected after NAT drop. Edge hedged upstream and backend applied op twice. We need a pragmatic plan beyond telling apps to be resilient.

rachel: yup. Two approaches we've kicked around: 1) client echoes a session token so reconnects correlate, 2) edge keeps tiny ephemeral state to correlate by src-ip+auth. Both have pros/cons.

omar: hybrid idea: gateway issues a short signed session token on first request (header `x-rw-session-init`). Client echoes back `x-rw-session` on reconnect. Token contains ts+nonce+hmac so any node can validate; no central store.

lee: that fixes cross-node reconnects. What about routes that can't resume because of side-effects? We should gate resume by route config `resume_policy: disabled|best_effort|strict` and `retry_mode: none|idempotent|resume`.

rachel: also add a small hedge-hold window when a session token is presented: hold hedging for `resume_hold_ms` (default 1500ms) while validating token. If token validates, suppress hedging. If not, proceed with normal hedging.

omar: security: bind token to auth-id when possible (HMAC over api-key-hash) and keep TTL short (e.g., 45s). Also rate-limit resume attempts per ip/key.

lee: observability: emit `edge.session_issued`, `edge.session_resume_attempt`, `edge.hedge_suppressed`. Console should show per-route resume success rate.

ci-bot: canary deploy started: `edge/session-resume@canary` (2 nodes) :rocket:

lee: action items:
- implement token gen/validate in ingress and unit tests for race reconnects (omar)
- proto changes for route flags and defaults (rachel)
- add metrics + console tile (lee)

omar: i'll open a minimal PR with token format example and tests.

rachel: i'll draft route proto and docs for ops.

lee: thanks all. We'll iterate on TTL/hold defaults after canary metrics. :thumbsup:
